context: Contain the failure at the guards-fix recipe level (e.g. run the skill-sync step with its exit status captured, print the notice naming the underlying error, and decide deliberately whether guards-fix then exits 0-with-notice or nonzero-after-summary). description: Successor of guards-fix-aborts-on-skill-sync-unreadable-tree (dropped 2026-07-31: its only rung, `make guards-fix`, is machine-dependent - wherever the skill-sync CLI is absent the target already exits 0 with a skip notice, so the rung was green on the unfixed tree in every environment except the one machine with the CLI installed; not falsifiable elsewhere). Reported failure (on a machine with skill-sync installed): guards-fix aborts at its final skill-sync step with 'unable to read tree <sha>'; the earlier regens have already landed but the completion summary never prints. Reproduced deterministically 2026-07-31 in a clean clone by pointing SKILL_SYNC at a stub that prints 'unable to read tree deadbeef' and exits 1: `make guards-fix SKILL_SYNC=<stub>` aborts with 'make: *** [Makefile:828: guards-fix] Error 2' before its 'guards-fix done' summary. Fix in the Makefile: when the skill-sync step fails, guards-fix must surface the failure text and still print its regenerated-artifact summary (skip-with-notice, or fail only after reporting) - without silently swallowing genuine skill-sync drift.
